Breakdown.theorem71_extended.summary: From a certificate in the sense of §7.3 it gives one $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ and a smooth nonzero profile of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry whose correction $v=W(S\theta,\cdot)-W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha$ satisfies (7.38), with the symmetries (7.39). Proved from the authors' library.
Breakdown.theorem71_extended.note:
This is our own statement of Theorem 7.1, written to keep everything the paper's theorem asserts about the chosen parameter. Assume a certificate in the formal sense of §7.3. The formal statement gives one parameter $\alpha$ in the parameter set and a pair $(W,q)$ that is jointly smooth, solves the profile equation (1.2) with period $S(\alpha)>0$ and the identity isometry, is divergence free and not identically zero, and obeys $|
abla^jW(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-1-j}$ for $j=0,1,2$ and $|
abla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. For the correction $v(	heta,y)=W(S	heta,y)-W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha(	heta,y)$ it gives membership in the perturbation class $\mathcal D^\Gamma_S$, the bound $\|v\|_w^2+\omega^2| eta^{\mathrm a}(\alpha)|^2\le4\varepsilon^2$, the bound $\sup_	heta\|v(	heta)\|_{\dot H^1}\le M$ and the pin values $\ell(v)= ar\ell(\alpha)$, which are the three parts of (7.38). It also gives $W(s+	heta_0S,Ry)=RW(s,y)$ for every $(R,	heta_0)\in\Gamma$, which is (7.39) after replacing $y$ by $Ry$. The weighted norm is stated together with the finiteness of its integrand, and matrix norms are Frobenius norms. Compared with the paper, the conclusion asserts more about the profile (decay of $
abla^2W$ and of $
abla q$), and the hypothesis is the formal certificate, which asks for more regularity of the approximate profiles than §7.3 does. The authors' own formal Theorem 7.1 concludes only that some weak profile exists; this statement keeps the parameter, the period, the correction and its bounds.

Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.title: The conclusion of Theorem 7.1
Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.source:
def ExtendedConclusion {k : ℕ} (d : ExtendedCertificateData k) : Prop :=
  ∃ α ∈ d.params, ∃ (W : ℝ → Space → Space) (q : ℝ → Space → ℝ),
    IsIdentityProfile (d.period α) W q ∧
    CorrectionBounds d.symmetries (d.period α) (d.profile α)
      d.multiplierWeight (d.multiplier α) d.pin (d.targetGap α)
      d.weightFn d.sizeBound d.supBound W ∧
    PrescribedSymmetries d.symmetries (d.period α) W
Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.summary: The conclusion of Theorem 7.1 for one certificate: some $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ and a smooth nonzero profile of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry whose correction satisfies (7.38) and whose symmetries are (7.39).
Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.note:
For a certificate, this proposition asserts that there are a parameter $\alpha$ in the parameter set and a pair $(W,q)$ with three properties. First, $(W,q)$ is a smooth nonzero profile with period $S(\alpha)$ and the identity isometry, with decay of $W$, $
abla W$, $
abla^2W$ and $
abla q$. Second, the correction $v=W(S	heta,\cdot)-W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha$ lies in the perturbation class and satisfies the weighted bound, the uniform $\dot H^1$ bound and the pin values of (7.38). Third, $W$ has every symmetry prescribed by $\Gamma$, as in (7.39). It is a definition of what Theorem 7.1 asserts, used by our two statements above.

Theorem11.theorem11Space.title: Theorem 1.1 on R³, conditional form
Theorem11.theorem11Space.source:
/-- The requested endpoint `Theorem11Space`, the first part of
`theorem11SpaceBlowup`. Conditional on the profile premise `IsLibraryProfile W q P R A`: a smooth
pair (W, q) on ℝ × R³, not identically zero, solving the profile equations (1.2)
(the similarity residual vanishes and div W = 0), periodic up to the isometry
R with period P > 0, W(s+P, y) = R W(s, R⁻¹y), with the decay bounds
‖∇ʲW(s,y)‖ ≤ A (1+|y|)^-(j+1) for j = 0, 1, 2 and |∇q(s,y)| ≤ A (1+|y|)^-3.
This is the premise of the authors' route (`Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile`);
it is stronger than the printed hypothesis (1.2)-(1.3), see
`Theorem11.OpenTarget.PaperSpace`.
Under it: one smooth finite-energy solution on [0,1) from a compactly supported
datum ε-close to W(0) in Ḣ¹, with the two-sided rate c(1-t)^(-1/4) ≤ ‖∇u(t)‖₂ ≤
C(1-t)^(-1/4) and the self-similar convergence rate (1-t)^κ. -/
theorem theorem11Space : Theorem11Space := by
  intro W q P R A h ε hε
  obtain ⟨u₀, u, p, c, C, κ, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h9, h10, h11, h12, h13, -, -⟩ :=
    theorem11SpaceBlowup W q P R A h ε hε
  exact ⟨u₀, u, p, c, C, κ, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h9, h10, h11, h12, h13⟩
Theorem11.theorem11Space.summary: Conditional on the profile premise (with $|\nabla q|\le A(1+|y|)^{-3}$): for every $\varepsilon>0$, one smooth finite-energy solution on $[0,1)$ from a compactly supported datum near $W(0)$, with $\|\nabla u(t)\|_2\sim(1-t)^{-1/4}$ and self-similar convergence.
Theorem11.theorem11Space.note:
Our statement of Theorem 1.1 on $\mathbb R^3$ in its global form, conditional on the profile premise. Premise (the profile premise of the authors' route): a smooth pair $(W,q)$ on $\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3$, not identically zero, solving the profile equations (1.2) with $\operatorname{div}W=0$, recurrent with period $P>0$ up to a linear isometry $R$, $W(s+P,y)=RW(s,R^{-1}y)$, with $|
abla^jW(s,y)|\le A(1+|y|)^{-1-j}$ for $j=0,1,2$ and $|
abla q(s,y)|\le A(1+|y|)^{-3}$. This is stronger than the printed (1.2)–(1.3): the bounds on $
abla^2W$ and $
abla q$ are assumed, and Remark 1.2's upgrade is not formalised. Under it, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the formal statement gives a smooth compactly supported divergence-free datum $u_0$ with $\|
abla(u_0-W(0))\|_2<\varepsilon$, one smooth solution $(u,p)$ of the Navier–Stokes equations with viscosity one on $[0,1)	imes\mathbb R^3$ with datum $u_0$, whose energy $\int|u(t)|^2$ is bounded on all of $[0,1)$, and constants $0<c\le C$, $0<\kappa<1/4$ with $c(1-t)^{-1/4}\le\|
abla u(t)\|_2\le C(1-t)^{-1/4}$ and $\|
abla(\sqrt{1-t}\,u(t,\sqrt{1-t}\,\cdot)-W(-\log(1-t)))\|_2\le C(1-t)^\kappa$ for all $t\in[0,1)$. Compared with the paper, the conclusion is the paper's construction on $\mathbb R^3$ with blow-up time one, its two-sided rate and its convergence in self-similar variables; the paper measures the error in the original variables against (1.4), which this statement does not restate, and the hypothesis is the stronger profile premise. The authors' own formal Theorem 1.1 concludes only that no global smooth solution of bounded energy exists; this statement keeps the solution.

Theorem11.theorem11SpaceBlowup.title: Blow-up on R³ with uniqueness
Theorem11.theorem11SpaceBlowup.source:
/-- Theorem 1.1 on R³, conditional on the profile premise.

Conditional on the profile premise `IsLibraryProfile W q P R A`: a smooth
pair (W, q) on ℝ × R³, not identically zero, solving the profile equations (1.2)
(the similarity residual vanishes and div W = 0), periodic up to the isometry
R with period P > 0, W(s+P, y) = R W(s, R⁻¹y), with the decay bounds
‖∇ʲW(s,y)‖ ≤ A (1+|y|)^-(j+1) for j = 0, 1, 2 and |∇q(s,y)| ≤ A (1+|y|)^-3.
This is the premise of the authors' route (`Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile`);
it is stronger than the printed hypothesis (1.2)-(1.3), see
`Theorem11.OpenTarget.PaperSpace`.

Under this premise, for every ε > 0, in the paper's words: there exist a divergence-free datum u₀ in C_c^∞(R³; R³), within ε of the
profile's slice W(0) in the Ḣ¹ seminorm, and a smooth solution u of the
Navier–Stokes equations on [0,1) × R³ with datum u₀ and finite energy, which
blows up at time 1: there exist κ in (0, 1/4) and constants 0 < c ≤ C with
c (1-t)^(-1/4) ≤ ‖∇u(t)‖_{L²} ≤ C (1-t)^(-1/4), and, in self-similar variables,
‖∇(√(1-t) u(t, √(1-t) ·) - W(-log(1-t)))‖_{L²} ≤ C (1-t)^κ, for t in [0,1).
Moreover every smooth finite-energy solution with datum u₀ on an interval
[0,T), T ≤ 1, is u there, and no smooth solution with datum u₀ and finite
energy exists on the closed interval [0,1]. -/
theorem theorem11SpaceBlowup : Theorem11SpaceBlowup := by
  intro W q P R A h ε hε
  have hp := libraryProfile_to_similarity h
  obtain ⟨d⟩ := theorem11SpaceCore W q P R A h ε hε
  obtain ⟨hP, -, -, -, -, hper, hn, -, -⟩ := h
  have hslab := fun T : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 =>
    Theorem11Core.local_physical_quantitative W q A ε hp d T T.2.1 T.2.2
  choose U p hs h0 hE hB hread hquant using hslab
  have hagree : ∀ S T : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) (min (S : ℝ) T), U S t = U T t :=
    fun S T => Theorem11Core.local_velocity_unique d.state (hs S) (hs T) (hread S) (hread T)
  have hsol := glued_solution d.datum U p hs h0 hagree
  have hE0 : (∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (‖d.datum x‖ ^ 2)) ≠ ⊤ := by
    obtain ⟨B, hB0⟩ := hE (slabEnd 0)
    have h00 := hB0 0 ⟨le_rfl, (slabEnd 0).2.1.le⟩
    rw [h0] at h00
    exact ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top h00
  have henergy : UniformFiniteEnergyBefore 1 (gluedVelocity U) := by
    refine ⟨(∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (‖d.datum x‖ ^ 2)).toReal, ENNReal.toReal_nonneg,
      fun t ht => ?_⟩
    have hle := Theorem11Energy.energy_le_initial (hs (slabEnd t)) (hE (slabEnd t))
      ⟨ht.1, (lt_slabEnd ht).le⟩
    rw [h0] at hle
    exact hle.trans (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hE0).ge
  -- Any smooth finite-energy solution with the same datum agrees with a slab.
  have hunique : ∀ (S : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (v : Velocity) (q' : Pressure),
      Breakdown.IsSolutionOn S v q' → Breakdown.EnergyBoundedOn S v → v 0 = d.datum →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) S, v t = U S t := by
    intro S v q' hvS hvE hv0 t ht
    have heq := Breakdown.eq_of_isSolutionOn (hs S) hvS (hE S) hvE (hB S)
      (by rw [h0 S, hv0])
    exact (heq t ht).symm
  let C : ℝ := max d.lowerConstant (max d.upperConstant d.errorConstant)
  have hcu : d.upperConstant ≤ C := (le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)
  have hce : d.errorConstant ≤ C := (le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)
  refine ⟨d.datum, gluedVelocity U, gluedPressure p, d.lowerConstant, C, d.exponent,
    d.datum_test.1, d.datum_test.2.1, d.datum_test.2.2,
    d.initial_gradient_finite, d.initial_gradient_close, hsol, henergy,
    d.lowerConstant_pos, le_max_left _ _, d.exponent_pos, d.exponent_lt_quarter,
    ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro t ht
    obtain ⟨hf, _, hlo, hhi, _, _⟩ := hquant (slabEnd t) t ⟨ht.1, (lt_slabEnd ht).le⟩
    have hdt : 0 ≤ 1 - t := by linarith [ht.2]
    exact ⟨hf, hlo, hhi.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcu (Real.rpow_nonneg hdt _))⟩
  · intro t ht
    obtain ⟨_, _, _, _, he, hconv⟩ := hquant (slabEnd t) t ⟨ht.1, (lt_slabEnd ht).le⟩
    have hdt : 0 ≤ 1 - t := by linarith [ht.2]
    exact ⟨he, hconv.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hce (Real.rpow_nonneg hdt _))⟩
  · intro T hT1 v q' hv hvE t ht
    obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ : ∃ S : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, (S : ℝ) = (t + T) / 2 :=
      ⟨⟨(t + T) / 2, by linarith [ht.1, ht.2], by linarith [ht.2]⟩, rfl⟩
    have htS : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) S := ⟨ht.1, by rw [hS]; linarith [ht.2]⟩
    have hST : (S : ℝ) < T := by rw [hS]; linarith [ht.2]
    rw [gluedVelocity_eq U hagree S htS]
    exact hunique S v q' (isSolutionOn_of_before hv hST) (energyBoundedOn_of_before hvE hST)
      (funext hv.initial) t htS
  · rintro ⟨v, q', hv, hvE⟩
    refine Theorem11Core.no_continuous_continuation W q P R A hP hp hper hn d
      hv.smooth_velocity.continuousOn (fun t ht => ?_)
    obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ : ∃ S : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, (S : ℝ) = (t + 1) / 2 :=
      ⟨⟨(t + 1) / 2, by linarith [ht.1], by linarith [ht.2]⟩, rfl⟩
    have htS : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) S := ⟨ht.1, by rw [hS]; linarith [ht.2]⟩
    have hS1 : (S : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by rw [hS]; linarith [ht.2]
    have hvt := hunique S v q' (isSolutionOn_of_through hv hS1)
      (energyBoundedOn_of_through hvE hS1) (funext hv.initial) t htS
    rw [hvt]
    exact hread S t htS
Theorem11.theorem11SpaceBlowup.summary: Conditional on the profile premise: everything in our Theorem 1.1 on $\mathbb R^3$, and every smooth finite-energy solution from $u_0$ on $[0,T)$, $T\le1$, equals $u$ there, and no smooth finite-energy solution from $u_0$ exists on $[0,1]$.
Theorem11.theorem11SpaceBlowup.note:
This adds to our Theorem 1.1 on $\mathbb R^3$ the two facts that make $t=1$ a blow-up time. Premise (the profile premise of the authors' route): a smooth pair $(W,q)$ on $\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3$, not identically zero, solving the profile equations (1.2) with $\operatorname{div}W=0$, recurrent with period $P>0$ up to a linear isometry $R$, $W(s+P,y)=RW(s,R^{-1}y)$, with $|
abla^jW(s,y)|\le A(1+|y|)^{-1-j}$ for $j=0,1,2$ and $|
abla q(s,y)|\le A(1+|y|)^{-3}$. This is stronger than the printed (1.2)–(1.3): the bounds on $
abla^2W$ and $
abla q$ are assumed, and Remark 1.2's upgrade is not formalised. Under it, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the formal statement gives the datum $u_0$, the solution $u$ on $[0,1)$ and the constants of that theorem, with the two-sided rate and the self-similar convergence; moreover every smooth solution with datum $u_0$ and finite energy on an interval $[0,T)$ with $T\le1$ coincides with $u$ there, and no smooth solution with datum $u_0$ and finite energy exists on the closed interval $[0,1]$. The solution is built by gluing the library's solutions on $[0,T]$, $T<1$, using the library's uniqueness, with pressures normalised to vanish at the origin; the energy bound up to time one comes from the authors' localized energy estimate.

comparisons.note: Theorem 7.1 gives one $\alpha$, a profile of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry, (7.38) for the correction and the symmetries (7.39). Our formal statement gives all of these for the same $\alpha$ and the same profile, and adds decay of $\nabla^2W$ and $\nabla q$; its hypothesis is the formal certificate, which asks for more regularity of the approximate profiles than §7.3. So the conclusion is at least as strong and the hypothesis is the formal one.

Our formal statement keeps the chosen parameter, the period, the correction and the three bounds of (7.38) with the symmetries (7.39), and adds decay of $\nabla^2W$ and $\nabla q$; it assumes the formal certificate, which asks for more regularity than §7.3.

The sentence combines Proposition B.14 with Theorem 7.1 and Corollary 7.2. Our formal statement combines the cell conditions with Theorem 7.1 and keeps the profile with (7.38) and (7.39); it stops before Corollary 7.2, whose formal form is the nonexistence statement tied to this sentence.

Theorem 1.1 assumes a profile in the sense of (1.2)–(1.3) and states the construction on $\mathbb R^3$ and on the torus. Our formal statement assumes the stronger profile premise, with bounds on $\nabla^2W$ and $\nabla q$, and gives on $\mathbb R^3$ one smooth finite-energy solution on $[0,1)$ with the two-sided rate and the convergence in self-similar variables; the torus part and the error in the original variables remain open targets.
The phrase gives the profile hypothesis. Our formal statement assumes more: the bounds on $\nabla^2W$ and on $\nabla q$ are part of its premise, where the paper has only (1.3) and Remark 1.2.

transposeApply.question: Why did Comparator reject the standalone readable cell file against the library on one definition?
transposeApply.answer: The two definitions elaborate to the same type and the same value except for the name of one auxiliary proof: the proof that 1 + 1 is at least two, inside the numeral 2 that is the exponent of the Euclidean space. Lean stores that proof as an auxiliary theorem named after the first declaration of its module, so it is named differently in the two files. Renaming it makes the two constants identical. A second comparison of all 1,923 library constants used by the statements of the three cell theorems, with auxiliary proofs identified by their statements, found every one identical. No mathematical statement differs.
